learning_outcomes.text: Understand the theory and basic notions of technical drawing and its related standards.
Know the main elements and modules of machines and mechanical systems.
Draft technical drawings based on their application and the manufacturing processes needed to realize the parts.
Compare design alternatives for mechanical systems based on external requirements.
Develop adequate independence in the evaluation of mechanical systems for a correct design and representation.
Develop fluency in the representation of mechanical systems (both in hand-sketching and with the help of software tools).
Be able to provide new concepts and design solutions for components and assemblies considering the changing external requirements.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the basics of technical drafting
Relationships with production and control processes
Couplings for torque transmission (keys, cotter, splined shaft, pins)
Application examples of bearings and seals
Methodology for choice and mounting of bearings and seals
Machine drawing basis: standards and standardization authorities
Isometric views: European system (first angle projection)
Isometric views: American system (third angle projection)
Designation and Relative Positions of Views
Sectional view types: Full Section, Half Section, Local Section
Dimensioning: definitions (dimension line, projection line, termination, value of the dimension)
Special indications (Diameters, Chords, Archs, Angles, Radii, Chamfers, Tapered, etc.)
Arrangement of dimensions (chain dimensioning, parallel dimensioning, combined dimensioning, co-ordinate dimensioning)
Materials and technologies: chipping, grinding, milling, refining, etc.
Limits, Dimensional tolerances, and fits: Fundamental tolerances, Fundamental deviations, Method of placing limit dimensioning
Indicating Dimensional tolerances on the drawings
Indicating geometrical tolerances on the drawings
Indicating surface roughness on the drawings
Screw thread and Screwed fasteners: Introduction and nomenclature
Shaft couplings: keys, Cotters, Pins, and Splined shafts
Bearings and seals: Introduction and classification
Seals (o-ring, v-ring, rotary shaft seal, etc.)

assessment_methods.method: 3 technical questions related to course topics

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a 3-hour writing assignment with three requests: a technical drawing of an assembly, a technical drawing of a component, and three technical questions. The exam result is calculated by summing the results from the drawing part and the technical questions. Students can request an optional oral exam, which may increase or decrease the written exam grade, or result in failure. Access to the oral exam is granted only after passing the written test.
